chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:

I asked him about the skin of the dead animal (beast) that has been salted, which is the kaimukh (leather), so he granted permission (deemed it permissible) in it, and said, 'If you do not touch it, it is better.'
ai.seo_question: Is the skin of a dead animal permissible if it is salted?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of *kaimukh* (salted skin of a *maytah*) as a distinct category of purity, where the Imam permits its use but recommends avoiding direct contact to preserve ritual cleanliness. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that the process of salting can purify the skin, distinguishing it from the flesh which remains impure, and highlights the nuance between absolute impurity (*najis*) and recommended caution (*awla*).
